messages:
sre-oncall: :rotating_light: Alert from telemetry: gpu-node-47 generating repeated Xid driver resets (Xid 13/31) and kernel OOMs across multiple containers. Serving runtime reports per-host OOMs and a spike in GPU ECC correctable errors. Paging oncall.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-041 (gpu-node-47). Auto-evac policy triggered for pods with evictionPriority=high. Notifying infra and hw oncall.

ana: I'm taking the lead — ana (sre). Actions: cordon + drain node, shift live traffic to fallback pool, collect dmesg + nvidia diagnostics, avoid immediate reboot if possible.

ana: ```bash
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon gpu-node-47
kubectl drain gpu-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force -n inference
```

jordan-cs: Notifying impacted customers: Cust-A and Cust-B seeing elevated errors. Sending brief now, will update with impact numbers. :mailbox_with_mail:

emily: grabbing kernel logs and nv-smi output now. running: `dmesg | tail -n 120` and `nvidia-smi -q --all > /tmp/nvsi.out`

emily: dmesg snippet: ```
[1767722222.324] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, pid=4312 faulted address 0x7f8a...
[1767722222.325] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4312 (redwood-runtime) score 988 or sacrifice child
[1767722230.128] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU reported ECC single-bit error
```

mike: infra-eng here. I see driver version 525.60 on that node. Before reboot, I'll try a driver module reload and restart container runtime to see if resets stop. Capturing: `/var/log/messages`, `journalctl -k -u kubelet`, and `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log`.

ana: please do modprobe unload/load first. If Xid persists then we escalate to hardware. Don't reboot the node unless we have no other recourse (customers still routed to fallback).

mike: ran: `sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia` then `sudo modprobe nvidia` and `systemctl restart containerd`. Driver reload completed at 1767722320. Xid resets continued afterwards (multiple entries in dmesg).

ops-bot: Telemetry update: p95 latency for model `redwood-large-v1` increased from 350ms -> 2.6s; automatic fallback to `redwood-medium-quant` initiated for some requests to preserve availability. Error rate up 1.2%.

jordan-cs: Customer update: Cust-A seeing ~6% failed requests, Cust-B intermittent timeouts. They're asking for ETA. I told them we're investigating and shifting traffic to fallback models; will follow up after diagnostics.

emily: collected process core backtrace of runtime pid 4312 (attached snippet): ```
#0  0x00007f8a12ab in gpu_process_call +0x34
#1  0x000056ab3bcd in runtime_worker
#2  0x00007f8a34d in start_thread
```
Noting repeated GPU faults immediately preceding SIGSEGV/OOM in container.

ana: logs collected under /tmp/inc-1767722222/ on node; uploaded to s3 at s3://redwood-incident-logs/inc-1767722222/. Links: <https://s3.redwood/internal/inc-1767722222/>

brad-hw: brad-hw here. From ECC single-bit spikes and persistent Xid after driver reload, I recommend isolating node and scheduling a hardware swap for the GPU(s). We'll cordon the host for a soak and schedule spare GPU swap tomorrow morning unless infra wants it sooner.

mike: agreed. For immediate mitigation we have drained high priority pods and shifted traffic. Will keep one lower-priority worker on node to collect telemetry until hardware team arrives.

ana: customer impact tally (so far): total request failures across platform +0.9%, p95 latency delta +2.25s for heavy model routes. A/B routing reduced user-facing errors but increased latency for some customers. Documenting in incident timeline.

jordan-cs: CS note: Cust-B wants an ETA and is asking whether this is a recurring issue. They'll want root cause and mitigation timeline. I'll keep them on standby.

emily: added extra telemetry traces and enabled extended nvidia debug logging (NVreg_RestrictProfilingToAdmin=0 and nvidia-debug enabled). Dumped smi snapshots every 10s to s3.

mike: created short-term alert to escalate if Xid rate > 5/min for more than 2 consecutive minutes. Also opened infra ticket TCK-8743 to track node replacement.

ops-bot: Actions recorded: cordon/drain done, driver reload attempted, telemetry fallback applied, hardware escalation requested. Incident level: SEV2.

ana: handoff time — 1767722560. I'm off for the next 2 hours; handing to mike for night monitoring. Handoff notes: logs at s3, node quarantined, hardware swap requested, keep customers updated if error rate >1% or p95 >1s.

mike: ack — taking over. Will monitor Xid rate and follow up with hardware on replacement. If resets continue post-driver-swap, we'll schedule full node reboot and escalate to vendor support. Leaving a short runbook in the incident doc. :thumbsup:

brad-hw: I'll aim to get a spare GPU mounted and test in staging before swap. If we see similar ECC errors in staging with same driver, we'll route rack traffic to alternate hosts next maintenance window.

ana: thanks team. Closing immediate paging loop; we'll reopen if conditions worsen or if hardware reports different. /handoff

mike: last check @1767722560 — Xid events reduced after drain but not eliminated; continuing watch.
